commit_attribution: The primary human-authorized operator session performed all steps directly: bootstrap, CPIPC validation, connecting the genuine YubiKey on request, all evidence authoring, commits. Two privileged read-only commands were executed via macOS's native Authorization Services GUI dialog (osascript ... with administrator privileges) at the operator's own machine, never through this session's terminal/chat -- no admin password was seen, requested in chat, echoed, or logged. No delegated worker was used this phase. DELEGATED .3 FINALIZATION / COMMIT / PUSH: UNAUTHORIZED preserved.
summary: CPIPC successor validated (direct successor of the deployment-state IV phase, no discrepancy). Orientation reconfirmed the predecessor's INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED deployment state, clean working tree, origin/main..HEAD=0 at entry (C0 e44becc9). The operator was asked whether the genuine YubiKey was connected; it was not, so the operator connected it on request. The real, unmodified NativeCtap2Provider (no seam) then confirmed 1 device present -- HidDescriptor(vid=4176, pid=1026, product_name='YubiKey FIDO') -- and a live Ctap2.get_info() call showed FIDO_2_1 support with clientPin/pinUvAuthToken/up/rk all true, matching the certified hpac.fido2.uv_presence.v2 profile's hardware expectations: genuine hardware VERIFIED PRESENT. Before any ceremony step, deployment freshness and credential validity were revalidated: two privileged READ-ONLY commands (HumanPrincipalRegistryStore.production().resolve_credential on the credential_id from the prior .1R.30R.5R.1 hardware-capability IV, and a full registry load) were executed via the macOS GUI admin-authorization dialog (0 mutations). Both showed the production human-principal registry is EMPTY (0 principals, 0 credentials) -- the prior real-hardware makeCredential exercised in .1R.30R.5R.1 produced only hardware-verification evidence, not a production enrollment transaction. Primary-source inspection of src/pcae/core/hpac_rhamp_enrollment.py confirmed credential enrollment is architecturally confined inside the non-agent-importable fence (HPAC-PAWA-REQ-084/085): its own docstring states ordinary agent/runtime/Gate/plugin/pcae-CLI code SHALL NOT import it, and enrollment authority originates solely from the standalone scripts/hpac_principal_admin.py, run directly by the deployment owner. This phase's authorized MAY-list lists only 'create/verify the real FIDO2 assertion' (an existing-credential getAssertion), never credential enrollment/makeCredential-to-registry, and the operator directive's own explicit 'NO AD-HOC CREDENTIAL ENROLLMENT' rule requires stopping before ceremony rather than inventing an enrollment path when enrollment would be required and is outside authorized scope. Accordingly the phase STOPPED before any ceremony step: no makeCredential, no getAssertion, no protected-presentation helper launch, no human election request, no PIN/touch request were performed; the connected YubiKey was used only for the two non-credential-bound capability checks above. The N-16-5 closure-criteria table was reconstructed per the directive's own template: 5/27 PASS (carried predecessor deployment verdict + mechanism-selection-only items), 1 FAIL (criterion 25, 'no unresolved N-16-5 blocker remains' -- this phase's own blocker C-1), 21 NOT ATTEMPTED/moot (every criterion downstream of a real positive ceremony, including the negative-case matrix, since none would change the verdict given C-1). N-16-5: NOT CLOSED. F-5: DEPLOYMENT VERIFIED -- CERTIFICATION BLOCKED. Runtime remained not_implemented/Observed/observe/unavailable, 0 plugins/capabilities throughout; no production/scripts/pyproject/contracts diff since C0; no existing test modified. Derived (not begun) the exact recommended successor: a narrowly-scoped, deployment-owner-run first-credential enrollment/bootstrap ceremony via scripts/hpac_principal_admin.py, after which this exact certification scope should be re-attempted unchanged. N-16-6/N-16-7 remain OPEN/UNTOUCHED and strictly out of scope.
derived_correctness: The credential-absence finding was independently corroborated by two separate methods, not asserted from a single source: (1) a direct resolve_credential() lookup against the specific credential_id named in the prior hardware-capability IV's own evidence file (rhamp_hardware_cert_30r5r1.json), returning not-found, and (2) an independent full registry load reporting principal_count=0/credential_count=0 -- the same conclusion from two different code paths through the real production HumanPrincipalRegistryStore, not a cached or predecessor-reported claim. The architectural-wall conclusion (enrollment outside agent scope) was independently verified by reading hpac_rhamp_enrollment.py's own module docstring directly rather than inferring it from PROJECT_STATUS.md prose. Hardware presence was independently verified via two separate live calls (available() and a raw Ctap2.get_info() against the actual opened device), not merely trusted from the operator's own statement that a key was connected.
